podcast.title: Considered "Too Pop for Alternative"
podcast.body: Paramore was listed among the artists considered "too pop to be alternative" by some segments of the alt-rock scene, encountering similar criticisms regarding their appeal. "and even Paramore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career and 360 Deal
podcast.body: Paramore, originating from a tiny town in Tennessee, signed a 360 deal with Fueled by Ramen, which had a deal with Atlantic Records (part of Warner Music Group). This deal provided them with new gear, a new van, and financial support for singer Hayley Williams' mother to continue Hayley's schooling while the band toured as she was still in high school. "Paramore is from a tiny town in Tennessee. They were originally signed to a label called Fueled by Ramen, who struck a deal with Atlantic Records, which is owned by the Warner Music Group, which is one of the major labels. Their deal was very 360."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Exception to Pop Punk Decline
podcast.body: Paramore was noted as an exception to the general decline of pop punk in the 2010s, demonstrating continued relevance in the genre. "We might point to Paramore, but a better example is probably Fallout Boy, who actually returned from Mahayatus in 2013 with an album that they called Save Rock and Roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Influenced by Blink-182
podcast.body: Paramore is mentioned as an artist who has been influenced by Blink-182, highlighting Blink-182's significant role in shaping the landscape of contemporary pop punk and alternative music. "Some 41 good Charlotte simple-plan panic at the disco, followed boy, headly, billy talent, you would meet six, paramour, you get the idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Moved Away from Emo Sound
podcast.body: Paramore was cited as a band that moved away from their original emo sound by the early 2010s, along with Fall Out Boy and Panic! at the Disco, contributing to the genre's temporary decline. This shift was part of a larger trend as fans and bands evolved, though emo later saw a strong revival mid-decade. "Followed boy moved away from their original emo sound as did Paramore and Panic at the disco."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Shift from Emo Sound
podcast.body: Paramore was noted as one of the bands that moved on to explore other sounds and styles, diverging from their original emo sound after the peak of third wave emo. "Others moved on to other sounds and styles, think panic at the disco and fallout boy in Paramore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Slow Development to Million-Selling Status
podcast.body: Paramore developed slowly, away from the mainstream spotlight, but by the time their third album was released, they were selling records by the millions. Their 360 deal is highlighted as an example of a successful arrangement for both the band and the label. "Paramore developed slowly, away from the mainstream, and by the time the dust cleared from their third album, they were selling records by the millions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
podcast.body: Paramore contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Black Paramore" Analogy
xref.body: Meet Me @ The Altar is likened to a "black version of Paramore," suggesting a similar pop punk style but with a distinct identity. "Meet me at the altar is like a block version of Paramore, except that they're all women and LGBTQ+."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Iconic Front Person and Entrepreneur
xref.body: Hayley Williams, the front person for Paramore, has achieved iconic status independently, extending her brand into various ventures. She launched a cosmetics line designed with Mac, which is accompanied by a TV series. Additionally, she has her own hair dye company, a line of tea, and scented candles. "She became an icon on her own with a line of cosmetics designed with Mac, there's a TV series that goes with that, a hair dye company, a line of tea, and even some scented candles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

xref.title: Influence on Pop Punk
xref.body: Blink-182 is considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century. Their style and career trajectory have left a significant mark on numerous artists across the genre, inspiring bands like Sum 41, Good Charlotte, Simple Plan, Panic! At The Disco, Fall Out Boy, Hedley, Billy Talent, You Me At Six, and Paramore. "Blink has to be considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Influences and Comparisons
xref.body: Avril Lavigne has been cited as an influence by contemporary artists such as Paramore, Fifi Dopson, and Sky Sweetenham. She has also been compared to Alanis Morissette and Courtney Love, being called the "millennial equivalent" to these influential figures. "Others have called her the millennial equivalent to Alannis Morsehset and Courtney Love."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Openness About Mental Health
xref.body: Hayley Williams has been candid about her struggles with mental health, particularly depression, which at one point led her to temporarily leave Paramore. Her openness has resonated with many fans. "Haley has also been open with her struggles with mental health, especially depression, something that caused her to leave Paramore for a short while."
